## 2026-10-23: field boxes drew at the world origin (hideable objects batched)

The user saw no dungeon boxes (containers) on the floors. Not the models, not a hide rule: the models build, are in the scene and are visible, but their meshes drew at the world origin.

**Cause.** `ObjectLayer.batchStatic` (`render/objectview.ts`) merges the objects that only change through `setVisible` (boxes, delayed objects: `hideableIndices`) per object, under the object root, with `StaticBatcher.build()`. `build()` switches the merged mesh's matrix updates off (`matrixAutoUpdate` and `matrixWorldAutoUpdate` false), so the mesh never gets its world matrix: it stays at identity. The geometry is in the object's frame (`space` = the inverse of the root's world matrix), so the merged mesh has to follow its root, as the parts did. `freezeStatic` then froze the identity matrix. Introduced by 3213a80 (2026-10-19, static batching); not by today's merges.

Found with a temporary Playwright spec (warp to Forest 1, read `view.objectLayer.models` and `view.field.objects.boxes`): the box root sat at the object (479.9, 33.1, 12.5) and its merged mesh at (0, 0, 0). After the fix the mesh has the root's world matrix and the crates show next to the path (screenshot taken in the worktree, not committed).

**Fix.** The own-batch loop sets `matrixAutoUpdate` and `matrixWorldAutoUpdate` back on for the merged meshes before they are added under the root; `freezeStatic` at the end of `batchStatic` computes and freezes their world matrices. The shared batches (world-space geometry, no own transform) were already right.

**Exe.** The box object is TObjContainerItem / TObjContainerBase (ctor FUN_0064deb4 / FUN_0064ee44, model 1 or 2), as before: `formats/objectmodels.ts` `containerSpec`. Forest 1 `map_forest01_00o.dat` has 50 box objects (0x0088 / 0x0092), all group 0 (not delayed), all with a model; the BML and XVM names are in `data.gsl`.

**ASSUMED.** None new: the crate placement is the object's position and yaw as before. The screenshot check put the player inside a crate (the spawn helper skips the collision test), so the outside view was checked only by the two facing shots.

**Tests.** `node tests/batching.test.ts` (new section: an own-batched object keeps its world matrix; the test fails without the fix), `node tests/objectcollision.test.ts`, `node tests/waves.test.ts`, `node tests/townfield.test.ts`, `node tests/drops.test.ts` all pass; `tsc --noEmit -p client` clean. Chrome: the Playwright check used the shared Vite and newserv; no spec is committed.

**Left.** The other hideable objects (the delayed ones, `construct`) take the same path and are fixed by it, but not seen in Chrome. The own path merges one mesh per object: a floor with many boxes makes many small draws (not measured).

## 2026-10-23: Mac function-key bar (F1..F12 buttons, web convenience)

On a Mac the top row of keys is brightness and volume, so F1..F12 reach the browser only with fn held. The game's F-key hotbar and the Alt+F emote keys could not be used from the keyboard. This is a browser convenience for the web port, not exe behaviour: the exe takes the F keys from the keyboard as usual.

**Game side (read, not changed).** The game reads keys as DOM key names, lower-cased, in the held-key sets of the views (`input/keyconfig.ts` KEYS; the hotbar is entries 20..31 = F1..F12, `input/keyconfig.ts` header; `formats/emotes.ts` ALT_EMOTE_ORDER starts with f1..f12). The Alt emotes test `keys.has('alt')` in the poll (`render/lobbyview.ts`), so Alt is a held key like the others. The on-screen pad (`input/virtualpad.ts`, `ui/webcontrols.ts` KeyFeed) already dispatches KeyboardEvents on the canvas, and that path is reused.

**Ported (web only).**
- `input/fkeys.ts` (new, pure): `isMacPlatform` (navigator platform, userAgentData; iPad in desktop mode and iPhone excluded), `fkeysShown` (stored "1" / "0", else the Mac default), `fKeyEventInit` (key and code F<n>, altKey), `holdRemaining` (the 120 ms floor, `FKEY_HOLD_MS`).
- `ui/webcontrols.ts`: `KeyFeed.send` takes altKey; `KeyFeed.pressFKey` sends F<n> down at pointer down and up at pointer up, never before 120 ms. With Option held and no physical Alt seen by the page it sends Alt down first and up last. A bar of 12 buttons top-left above the status window (`.wc-fkeys`, `ui/webcontrols.css`); `pointerdown` and `mousedown` are `preventDefault`ed and the canvas is refocused. An "Fn" toggle on the top strip shows and hides the bar; the choice is stored in localStorage `psobb.fkeys` (try/catch). The bar and the toggle are hidden where the touch pad shows.
- `tests/fkeys.test.ts` (platform detection, stored choice, event fields for F1..F12, hold timing); `client/e2e/fkeys-bar.spec.ts` (one spec: on a stubbed Mac the bar shows 12 buttons, a click on F1 gives keydown then keyup on the game canvas, 120 ms or more apart, and the canvas keeps the focus).

**ASSUMED.**
- The top band of the field canvas (above the status window, y < 37 virtual px, `classic/hud.ts` STATUS_WINDOW) is free of the game's own HUD. Checked against the HUD rectangles only, not on a screenshot.
- The field's viewer reads Alt from its held set the same way as the lobby (`render/lobbyview.ts`); only the lobby poll was read.
- The key is held while the pointer is down, and at least 120 ms: a click is a tap of 120 ms or more, a long press holds the key longer. The brief's fixed 120 ms tap was read as a minimum.

**Left.**
- The bar also shows on the title and login screens on a Mac (no per-screen suppression). Not checked there.
- Overlapping clicks on the same F key each send their own keydown and keyup; the game's held set can drop the key a little early when two presses overlap.
- The Alt emote path in the field was not run in Chrome. The e2e checks the F1 keydown and keyup only.

**Checks:** `node tests/fkeys.test.ts` passes; `node tests/controls.test.ts` passes (its newserv file check skipped: no vendor/newserv). `npx playwright test e2e/fkeys-bar.spec.ts` passes (1 test, Chrome, Vite on 5173 started by the config). `tsc --noEmit -p client` run with the main checkout's typescript: no errors in the touched files; the worktree has no node_modules, so the other tsc errors (three, vite, ImportMeta) are environment only.

## 2026-10-23: symbol chat cooldown on the End picker; End key traced to the quick menu

**What changed:** the picker's sends now wait for the chat cooldown (`is_chat_message_cooldown_over`, dump 679808). A decided row that comes too soon is kept and sent when the cooldown ends; Cancel drops it. The Home leaf's decided row now plays its sound only. `classic/symbolchat.ts`: `CHAT_COOLDOWN_FRAMES` (0x2d), `chatCooldownOver`, `chatCooldownTick`, and `SymbolRow.sound`. `classic/symbolchatlist.ts`: the decide callback returns whether the row was taken (the 'chat' window closes only then), and `close()`. `classic/field.ts`: the timer, the pending row, the send. `classic/lobby.ts`: `previewSymbol` plays `row.sound`. `tests/symbolchat.test.ts`: the cooldown, the row sound and the waiting list.

**Premise corrections (per the exe):**
- **The Home leaf does not send.** `ChatShortcutMenuWindow_Process_00758900` state 2 (dump 728744) calls `ProcessChatMessageType_0077d880` (dump 754383), which plays `PlayDirectionalSound(spec >> 5 & 0xf)` only when the present bit 0 is set. No `send_chat_message*` call is reached from the Home leaf, so the cooldown does not apply there. The earlier entry's balloon on a Home preview is not in the exe; the port now plays the sound only.
- **The End key is not a symbol picker in the exe.** Key role 14 (the enum name is `quickmenu`, dump 86172; the key config row is "Symbol Chat Open", `classic/keyconfig.ts` label 0x35) is tested in `unknown_handle_quickmenu` (dump 682493): `was_input_pressed(this, quickmenu)` calls `quick_menu_constructor` (dump 711543). So the End key opens the quick menu. The port has no quick menu (see the 2026-10-23 entries), so the 12-row End picker stays as a stand-in.
- **Dump 701678 comment is not the End path.** The comment at dump 701679 ("used for the following menus: symbol chat, guild card, simple mail, info board, options, quit game, symbol chat quickmenu, inventory purpose menu") introduces `ListWindowObject_ProcessInputAndRender_00734f3b` (701681), a generic list window. Its "symbol chat quickmenu" is a list window kind, not the End key's handler.

**Exe evidence** (`refsrc/original-psobb-client-source/src/Psobb.exe-05112026.c`, dump lines):
- Cooldown: `is_chat_message_cooldown_over` (679808) returns 1 when the short at `g_pUITextColorTable + 0x22` is below 1. `set_chat_message_cooldown_timer` (679819) writes 0x2d. `g_pUITextColorTable` is the quick menu object (`QuickmenuObject`, set at 677402). The timer is ticked down in `QuickmenuobjectHandleSelection_00716a60` (677732), only while the object's `+0x38` panel is set (the only decrement in the dump). Its callers: `send_chat_message_with_cooldown` (754191) and `send_chat_message_with_cooldown_optcall` (754207). A send that is refused (returns 0) leaves the row's 0x10 flag set, so the exe retries each frame until the cooldown is over (677766 path: the flag is cleared and the panel updated only after a send).
- Who reaches the cooldown: the quick menu object's chat panel (677766, `send_chat_message_with_cooldown(param_1 + 0xa0)`); the challenge player list's chat row (724794 in `ChallengePlayerListWindow_HandleInput_00752238`, 724757); the quick menu's trade path (732793 in `QuickMenuWindow_ProcessState_0075f09c`); and the Shift+F shortcut keys (`handle_chat_shortcuts` 674857 calls `use_chat_shortcut` 754183, which uses `send_chat_message_with_cooldown_optcall`). Text, word and symbol chats all pass through it.
- Who builds chat type 3 (`symbol_chat`, dump 86208): `ChallengePlayerInfoWindow_UpdateState_007138e0` (674657). Its state 1 (the "symbol chat case", dump 674690..674706) writes `**(param_1 + 0x30) = 3` and builds a `ChatShortcutMenu` (`ChatShortcutMenu_Constructor_007148c0`, 675688). The type-3 message is the list item the player picks (`get_value_from_selected_list_item`, the state's 0x2 branch near 674813); a valid row plays its sound (`ProcessChatMessageType_0077d880`, 674822). The send itself is the chat row's 0x10 flag (above).
- The 6x07 writer: `send_chat_message_symbol_chat` (754781) builds the subcommand from the entry's 0x2C..0x68 with `g_CurrentPlayerSlotIndex` and calls `checked_call_packet0x60_subcommand`, which runs it on the sender too.
- The shortcut slots (`get_chat_shortcut_optcall`, 0xa4 stride, 754134) hold the same chat_message records; the Chat > Shortcut leaf (0x11) that edits them is not ported, and its writer was not traced.

**Ported:**
- The End-key picker: a decided row is sent only when `chatCooldownOver(chatCooldown)`. The cooldown is set to 0x2d on each send and ticked down each 30 Hz field frame. While it runs, the row waits and the window stays open; the send happens when the timer ends, and Cancel drops the row. The sender's own balloon is shown at the send (as before).
- The Home leaf 0x12: a decided row plays `row.sound` (the spec's sound, only when the present bit is set). No send, no balloon, the window stays open.

**ASSUMED** (also marked in the code):
- The port ticks the cooldown every field frame. The exe ticks it only while the quick menu's chat panel `+0x38` is up (677732); the port has no such panel, so the timer runs in the field.
- The picker is a stand-in for the quick menu's chat row (End opens the quick menu in the exe). The picker's cooldown and its row flow follow the chat row path (677766 and the `ChallengePlayerInfoWindow` mode 1), but the link from role 14 to that window (through `quick_menu_constructor` and its tabs) is not traced.
- The chat window's 0x10 flag is treated as "send now" for symbol rows; the exe's retry on each frame is ported as the pending row.
- The text chat in the port has no cooldown. The exe's shared timer also gates text sends (`send_chat_message_text` via the same wrapper), so text chat should get the same gate when it is ported. Not done here.

**Tests:** `node tests/symbolchat.test.ts` (Node 24): ALL PASS (the earlier checks, plus the cooldown: the 0x2d timer, 45 ticks to over, the waiting list keeps its window; the row sound: present rows only). `tsc --noEmit -p client` (client/node_modules linked from the main checkout for the run, removed before the commit): no errors. Not run in Chrome (no Playwright, per the brief).

**Left (in order):**
1. The quick menu: `quick_menu_constructor` (711543), its tabs and the chat row, so that the End key opens it as the exe does. The picker then goes away (or becomes the chat row's list).
2. Text chat's cooldown (the same timer, `send_chat_message_text` path) and the Shift+F shortcut sends (`use_chat_shortcut`), which the port does not have yet.
3. The per-frame tick's real guard: the `+0x38` panel of the quick menu object.
4. The Home leaf's option list and item window (states 5..9) and the capture window, as before.
## 2026-10-23: Zonde family: the Gizonde chain's return and the Razonde caster emitter

**What changed.** The Zonde / Gizonde / Razonde objects were already ported (2026-10-20, "Technique visuals: Zonde, Grants, Megid, supports, special objects"). Re-traced against PsoBB.exe, two things differed and are fixed:
- **Gizonde's chain** (`combat/techlightning.ts gizondeStrike`, `render/techlightning.ts` case gizonde): the exe's return value decides the hit. A later pair with a missing entity, at zero distance, or both dead and flagged makes the visuals return 0, so the bolts drawn before that pair stay and **nothing** is hit. The port used to skip the pair and hit every target. A missing entity in the 6x47 list also no longer shifts the others up: the list keeps its order (null for a missing one).
- **Razonde's caster emitter** (`razondeStrike`): table[1]'s 60 frame emitter is at the caster's weapon position (`caster + 0x300`, the feet with the bloodstain offset ASSUMED zero), not the hand 20 above it.
- Player hit point (`render/combat.ts` `techWorld().point`): the player's point is the feet, not feet + 10. Gizonde's bolts and sparks and Megid's aim use it (the 2026-10-23 hit point entry: the player's box is the embedded one, position1 zero, so its centre is the feet). Megid's aim point moves 10 down with it.

**Exe evidence** (Ghidra dump `refsrc/.../Psobb.exe-05112026.c` names; asm from `objdump -d -M intel PsoBB.exe`):
- Zonde: `ZalureEffectEntity_Update_006f2840` (vtable 0x00b3e880). Constants 0x0096e050..0x0096e060. 14 points around the first target only, bolts to its origin (`+0x18` hit), SE 0x8f at its origin. No model constructor and no per-frame effect after the first update: nothing else to port.
- Gizonde: `TechniqueEffectEntity_Constructor_006e5520` (SE 0x90 + pitch by tier, asm-checked), `update_gizonde` 0x006e5890 (the hit loop: constructed and `is_npc_targetable`), `UpdateGizondeTechniqueVisuals_006e5954`. Tier thickness table at 0x006e5954 cases 0..5 (0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.6, 0.7, 5 + 0.5 + 0.5). Chain at asm 0x006e6021..0x006e6148: the vector is `box_{i+1}[idx_i].position2 - box_i[idx_{i+1}].position2` (the box indices are crossed; 0x2c per box, position2 at +0x1c), `call 0x6ea700` (constructed) on both, the flagged/targetable/dead test at 0x006e6082..0x006e60c1 (`jne 0x6e66b3`), the zero test against 0x0096d480 (= 0.0) at 0x006e613c..0x006e6148 (`je 0x6e66b3`). `0x6e66b3` is `return 0`.
- Razonde: `RafoieEffectEntity_Constructor_006ee674` (named Rafoie in the dump; `RafoieEffectEntity_Create_006ee600` is its creator). Step by level at asm 0x006ee767..0x006ee7a4: < 15 -> 5.4 (0x0096ddd8), 15..24 -> 8.1 (0x0096ddd0), 25..29 -> 10.8 (0x0096ddd4), >= 30 -> 5.4. Angle `+= 0x2aaa` per point, radius accumulates. 7 bolts of 5.0 (hold 6), tier 5 adds 0.5 ones. The caster-side particles in `RazondeEffectEntity_Update_006eeae0`: `create_particle_effect` at the caster's node for each table entry, and `create_particle_effect_ex(caster + 0x300, table[1], 0, 0x3c)`. No model in either function.
- The exe has no model entity for Zonde, Gizonde or Razonde (the "models" left in the Foie entry do not apply to this family).

**ASSUMED:**
- The Razonde table's other particles stay at the hand (the exe puts them at `pbVar1[0xe]`'s node, not decoded).
- `world.point` for a dead enemy returns null (the port's `live` test); the exe still draws a bolt to a constructed dead target and only the pair rule of both-dead stops the chain. Only the single-dead case differs.
- The chain uses one point per target; the exe's per-box indices (`idx` from the 6x47 entries) are not used, so multi-box targets' chain ends differ (no multi-box target is in a Gizonde's chain as far as the port knows).
- The exe runs the Gizonde visuals on the object's first update, one frame after the release; the port draws at once.

**Checks:** `node tests/techlightning.test.ts` (Gizonde: no target, zero distance, a bad pair in the middle and at the end (bolts kept, no hit), a clean chain of three, a missing first target; Razonde: caster emitter at the weapon position), `techfire`, `techniques`, `hitfx` pass; `tests/combat.test.ts` needs `vendor/newserv/build/newserv` (not built in this worktree, not run); client `tsc --noEmit` clean. Not run in Chrome.

**Left:** the Gizonde chain's per-box positions (the 6x47 box index) and the dead-target point; the Razonde table's non-first particles' node; the one-frame delay of the Gizonde visuals; the Zonde / Gizonde / Razonde casts' charge light (the cast light list is in techlightning.ts, not drawn).

## 2026-10-23: Team Member List: Send Mail and Meet the User ported (Sent Item left)

**Premise checked against the exe.** Two corrections to the entry above:
- **Send Mail is not the Simple Mail window (0x13).** The member's leaf is a short state run of `ChallengePlayerInfoWindow_ProcessState_0074d9ac` (dump 720824): state 0xb (line 720975) takes the text keyboard `CreateKeyboardControl_00756ab0` (dump 727622, `TKeyboardControl` with 0xb7 units, at get_gui_position(0xcf)); state 0xd (721010) moves it to 0xd0 and opens the confirm `ChatShortcutMenu_CreateWindow_00756a58` (dump 727577: title unitxt (11, 0x33), text (11, 0x52) "Are you sure?", at 0xa4, width 205). State 0xe (721018) decides: a cancelled confirm goes back to the keyboard (0xb); a decided one with value 0 calls `ChallengePlayerInfoWindow_SendActionError_0074e154` (dump 721260), which passes the searched card (+0x24) and the keyboard text to `SendPlayerSessionErrorMessage_008136f0` (dump 831429). That function is the 0x81 builder the Simple Mail DEVLOG describes (its first argument is the to-card, the text is cut at 0xab units). The dump's names for both are wrong (an "error" that sends mail); the bodies are the send. Any other value, or a Cancel, returns to the action list (state 4). So the port sends through the Simple Mail sender (`SimpleMailBox.send`), not through the 0x13 window.
- **Meet the User also reconnects.** State 0x12 (dump 721093) calls `ChallengePlayerInfoWindow_ProcessPhaseLabel_0074f028` (dump 722132). That function takes the 0x41 reply's location (the text at packet +0x24, cut at 0x44 units), keeps the last `,`-separated token (`DAT_00973b80` = 0x2c, `tools/exedata.py read 00973b80 u 1`) as `g_SinowberillChallengePhaseLabel` (dump 562747), and then calls `ShipConnectionManager_HandlePacket0x19_007d7640` (dump 812031) with the reply's embedded 0x19 (packet +0x14), which sends it on the connection and reconnects to the reply's address and port (packet +0x1c / +0x20). ## 2026-10-23: Vol Opt's monitor boxes (0xc2 is Vol Opt, not the Dragon); masked index and loop children

The brief called 0xc2 the Dragon. The exe and the port's `enemyids.ts` say otherwise: set type 0xc2 is TBoss3Volopt (Vol Opt, 1 + 6 + 24 + ... slots), and the Dragon is 0xc0 (TBoss1Dragon, ctor 0x00419214, table 0x009a39a0). The 0xc2 init found by the previous probe (site 0x004417e5, table `0x009a5100 + 0x2c * ([arg4] & 3)`) is the constructor of Vol Opt's monitors, which the port already models as `VoloptMonitor` (`combat/volopt.ts`, `shape = index & 3`, ctor 0x0044161C).

**The value the caller passes: the loop counter 0..23 (exe).**
- Vol Opt's vtable 0xaf5540 slot 4 is 0x0043c5d4, which calls the AI state function 0x0043c680 (the switch on `[ecx+0x32e]`). Mode 0 (0x0043c7fe..0x0043c94d) builds the arena: a 7-loop of 0x420-byte objects (0x004422d4), then a 24-loop from 0x0043c8a2: `call 0x005caba4` (alloc 0x39c), `call 0x0044161c` at 0x0043c92e. The loop counter is `[ebp-0x18]` (0x0043c944..0x0043c94d: `add $1`, `cmp $0x18`, `jl`), pushed as argument 4 (`push %ebx` at 0x0043c92a). The callee's `this` is the new object; argument 1 is Vol Opt itself (`esi = [ebp-0x14]`).
- The constructor 0x0044161c reads its argument 4 from `[ebp+0x14]` (0x00441657), masks it with `and $3` (0x004416b8), stores it at `+0x370` (0x004416bb), and uses it for the model (`0x009a5210[4*v]`, 0x00441727) and the box table (`lea 0x9a5100 + 44*v`, 0x004417d7..0x004417e2). Then `push $1` (count, 0x004417c4), `push table`, `call 0x007b9a88` (0x004417e5).
- So child k (k = 0..23, creation order) gets variant `k & 3`: each shape is used by 6 monitors (k = v, v+4, ...). The walk found no record field: the value is the caller's loop counter, not the set record.

**The rows (read with `tools/exedata.py read`, all centre (0,0,0), sphere, shape 0):** 0x009a5100 radius 20 flags 0x8005 (shape 0, the big monitor, `MONITOR_LOCK_Y` 43); 0x009a512c radius 10 flags 0x8003; 0x009a5158 radius 15 flags 0x8003; 0x009a5184 radius 10 flags 0x8003. All four have the 0x8000 targetable bit. They are the monitors' boxes, not body parts. The type 0xc6 (TBoss3VoloptMonitor) already links to row 0 (`0x441ea0 -> 0x441f1c`, a direct site with table 0x009a5100), which is the monitor's own function (ASSUMED: its default row).

**Generator (`tools/gen-collision-boxes.py`):**
- `step`: `andl $imm, %reg` on one leaf makes a leaf `('and', ('arg', k), mask)` (power-of-two masks only; any other `and` stays unknown). `indexed_site` accepts that leaf. The Vol Opt site 0x004417e5 now decodes as indexed (`mask 3`): 16 indexed sites (was 15), 27 undecoded (was 28), 246 tables (was 243).
- `index_mask`, `index_text`: `CollisionIndex.mask` (null for the record indexes, which are unchanged apart from the new field). The variant loop stops at mask + 1 (variants 0..3, not up to 16).
- `CHILD_CALLERS` (hand-read, checked by `main`): the monitor constructor 0x0044161C, its call site 0x0043C92E (must be an E8 call to it), the argument 4, the loop bound `cmp $0x18` at 0x0043C94A (checked by disassembly), count 24. The 0xc2 factory tree never reaches the site (the monitors are built by the AI's build state, not by the ctor's vtable slots), so `ENEMY_COLLISION_LINKS[0xc2]` stays null (that is correct: the root has no box table of its own in the exe).
- `CHILD_COLLISION_LINKS`: `0x00c2: { callee: 0x0044161c, count: 24, mask: 3, variants: { 0: 0x009a5100, 1: 0x009a512c, 2: 0x009a5158, 3: 0x009a5184 } }`.
- Regenerated `client/src/formats/collisionboxes.gen.ts` (diff: the new rows, the new site, the `mask` fields, the `CHILD_COLLISION_LINKS` block).

**Port:**
- `client/src/formats/enemyboxes.ts`: `childBoxTable(setType, child)` returns `{ table, rows }` for child k (`variants[k & mask]`), or null past the count, for a negative child, or for a set type with no children. The header explains it.
- No runtime consumer yet: the port's `VoloptMonitor` keeps its own hit test and HP. The rows are available for it, and for the monitors' box flags, when that is wired.

**The bosses 0xc8 / 0xca / 0xcb (exe).**
- 0xc8 (TBoss4DarkFalz): the candidate path is wrong. Vtable 0xaf6a20 is 0x1b8 bytes long; the address 0xaf6bd8 that the walk read as slot 0x1b8 is the vtable of a different class (its ctor 0x0044e57a stores 0xaf6bd8, and 0x0044e544 is that class's dtor, which frees its own +0x94 and +0xa8 members). The walker read past the end of 0xaf6a20, so 0x0044e544 is not the Dark Falz dtor and is not a box path. The real init 0x0045fca0 (table 0x009a67c8: radius 0, flags 0x807a) sits in the constructor 0x0045fb24 (vtable 0xaf7d60), which is called only from 0x0044c605 in the grid loop of 0x0044c430 (a placement routine: 0x0044c558..0x0044c614, rows of 10 up to 0x2d). That looks like the Darvants (0x1fd children), not the boss. Its caller chain above 0x0044c430 is not traced.
- 0xca (TBoss6PlotFalz, factory 0x0048d764): the ctor 0x0048d814 (vtable 0xaf9240) calls helpers 0x0048d038, 0x0048dafc, 0x0048db1c. The generator's tree from the factory (23 functions, depth 8) has no init call. The ctor's own sub-tree was not expanded (the function start for 0x0048d814 did not match the walker's table), so this is not final.
- 0xcb (TBoss7DeRolLeC, factory 0x004af5b8, ctor 0x004af634): the depth-8 tree is 1108 functions and reaches only the shared helpers 0x0051ff3c / 0x00521bbc / 0x00521c5c, which several set types reach. Not an own box; left.

**ASSUMED:**
- The monitor index is the loop counter (the monitor constructed k-th is `VoloptMonitor(k)`, `wall = k >> 2`, `shape = k & 3`). The exe agrees on the shape, the model table (0x9a5210) and the position table (0x9a51e0) use the same `& 3`, but the monitor's own index field is not read.
- `CHILD_CALLERS` is a hand-read exe fact: the generator checks the call and the loop bound, not the loop's start (0) and step (1), which are read from the same block by hand.
- The `and` leaf is a power-of-two mask on a single argument; any other `and` stays unknown.
- The walker still follows no branches. The Vol Opt path is straight-line within 0x44161c up to the init call (the model and table lines are not branched).
- Row 0 (0x009a5100) is the monitor's default: type 0xc6's own function 0x00441f1c sets it.
- 0x0044c430 is the entry of the Darvant grid loop's function (no padding seen between it and 0x0044c558); the Darvant reading of its children is a guess.

**Tests.** `node tests/objectcollision.test.ts` all checks passed (the Vol Opt monitor rows for k = 0, 5, 10, 23; radius 20 / 15; targetable; out-of-range and the no-children types; the root has no table; `CHILD_COLLISION_LINKS` fields). `node tests/techfire.test.ts` ok. `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` in `client/` clean. `client/node_modules` is a symlink to the main checkout's while testing and is removed before the commit. Not run in Chrome, no Playwright.

**Left:**
- The Dark Falz (0xc8) root box and the Darvants' box (0x9a67c8, radius 0, flags 0x807a) are not linked: their caller chain above 0x0044c430 is open.
- 0xca and 0xcb: the own init is not found (the ctor sub-trees need the walker's function starts fixed; the 0xcb tree is too generic at depth 8).
- Wire `childBoxTable(0xc2, i)` into the monitors' hit test, if the monitors' boxes should be used by the player's shots (the port's own hit test covers the monitors now).
- The 28 -> 27 undecoded sites: none is a boss factory's tree (the list in `--dynamic`).

**The zone bits (0x667bb5), exe evidence:**
- The object: entity type 0x57 (TObjTradeCollision, `formats/entitynames.ts`) is created by `CreateDerolleMapObject_00667ab4` (dump 531310). The factory table at 0x00a06f80 (16-byte records, read with `tools/exedata.py read`) has record id 87 at 0x00a06f90 with the factory 0x00667ab4 at 0x00a06f94 (ASSUMED reading of the record shape: id, factory, then two words). The dump's name `DerolleMapObjectVisibilityCheck_00667bb5` is the generic check; the dump's "Derolle" prefix is misleading.

This matches `entitynames.ts` (`TObjTradeCollision`: "Radius" is param 1). The port's `ObjectSet.params[0]` (f32 0x28) and `params[3]` (i32 0x34) are the two values.
- The check, from the disassembly of 0x667bb5..0x667c3a (not only the decompile): per slot 0..3: `GetPlayer_0068d5a8` null -> `ClearTradeStateFlag_00825ff4` (0x667bd9); `get_current_scene()` != 11 (`logged_in`, the scene enum at dump line 90487) or `g_QuestStarted` (0xa95624) == 1 or `player.floor_id_2` (+0x3f0) != `g_CurrentFloor` (0xaafca0) -> clear; else `vec3f_xz_dist_squared` (0x78ea50, player +0x38 and object +0x38) against `radius * radius` with `fcomps` / `sahf` / `jb` -> a distance below the radius clears (0x667bd9); otherwise, when param 4 is non-zero, `SetTradeStateFlag_00825fe0` (0x825fe0) sets the bit (0x667c33). - The reads: `ValidateTradePartner_00825a74` (dump 839080) and `ValidateLocalPlayerTradeState_00825bac` (dump 839190) call `IsTradeStateFlagSet_00825ac0` (dump 839115) and run `ProcessTradeAcceptance_00825ae4` on a CLEAR bit. ## 2026-10-23: trade zone, floors without a TObjTradeCollision stay permissive

Merge review of the trade zone port (`net/tradezone.ts`): with no type-0x57 object on the floor no
bit was ever set, so every field trade would be cancelled. newserv (`Map.cc`, TObjTradeCollision)
documents the object as disabling the Trade Window near it, so `TradeZone` now reads the bits only
once the floor has run a collision object check; a floor without one is permissive. ASSUMED: the
bits' default outside the city was not traced in the exe.

**Premise, checked:** the killer id is the monster name index (the classic PSO enemy list number, `unitxt_get_monster_name`). ## 2026-10-23: Simple Mail follow-ups (smut filter, arrival in a game, auto reply in the save)

Three open items of the Simple Mail entry above, traced in PsoBB.exe (Psobb.exe-05112026.c dump; Ghidra via `tools/ghidra/decomp.sh`; bytes via `objdump -d -M intel` and `tools/exedata.py`).

**Exe.**
- The 0x81 handler is not `handle_ship_packet0x81` at 0x00810083. That address is mid-function (Ghidra's FUN_00810030 starts before it), so the dump name is wrong. The real entry is **0x007c8dc4** (`push edi; push ebx; mov edi, ecx`; the caller's body is at 0x007c8dd6..0x007c8de7). It is the 0x81 entry of the (command, handler) pair table at **0x00a0f800** (8-byte stride; the pair at 0x00a0f9b8 = 0x81 / 0x007c8dc4, next to the 0x60 / 0x62 game entries, which suggests the same connection dispatch serves the game; the dispatcher that reads `[8*eax + 0xa0f804]` at 0x007c1a01 was not traced to its state gate, ASSUMED).
- Its body: `ProcessEntityNameWithShopItems(msg, msg)` with msg = packet + 0x5c (0x007c8dd6: `lea eax, [ebx+0x5c]`; `push eax; push eax; call 0x813a78`), then `call [edi+0x1e0d0]` = `unknown_packet_handlers[0x17]` (0x007c8de1), which is LAB_0081384c (set once in `init_ship_connection_manager`, 0x00797ce2: `mov [eax+0x1e0d0], 0x81384c`). The 0x17 handler runs FUN_00813a3c (the text check) and the store (FUN_0081386c, SE 0x586; the SE and the store are carried from the entry above, not re-decompiled here). The handler lives on the ship connection for the whole session: nothing clears slot 0x17.
- The filter (0x00813a78, ProcessEntityNameWithShopItems): `g_ShopDialogItemCount` (0x70ac58) < 1 → copy. Else for each item i (0x70ac60): `NormalizeAndFilterEntityName(item, out)` with EAX = `_Dest` (the working copy) and EDX = out (0x813ab0..0x813ad0), then `_Dest = out`. The item list is `g_ShopDialogItemList`, loaded by `InitializeShopDialog_0070ac88` (0x0070ac88, reached from the init table at 0x009ff7a8; the call is not in the code, ASSUMED: a start-up / session init step).
- The list file is `g_ShopDialogFilePath` = **"smutdata.prs"** (string at 0x0096ee00). It is read with the unitxt parser (`ParseUnitxtFileList_0070b084`): groups of strings, each group ended by an empty string. The port's `parseUnitxt` reads the same layout.
- Tables (read from the exe; the values are `FILTER_SYMBOLS` and `KATAKANA_FULL` in simplemail.ts): symbols 0x00980980 (16 entries of 4 units, stride 8: ASCII and fullwidth punctuation, 64 units in all) → spaces in the normalized text; halfwidth katakana FF66..FF9D → 0x00980a00 (56 units); the replacement pattern `g_ShopNameReplacementPattern` 0x00980a80 = "#!@%" x 8.
- Normalization (0x813b18): U+3000 → space; ASCII capitals → lower case; fullwidth FF21..FF3A → ASCII lower case (`- 0xfec0` gives 0x61..), FF41..FF5A → ASCII (`- 0xfee0`); katakana when unchanged; the symbol tables → space. The word match is on the normalized text N (leading and trailing space); the replacement writes `pattern[j]` for each non-space unit j of the word, into N and into the text O (O[i] is N[i+1]). The last match is replaced and the word is searched again. A tab starts a second pass: the tab's unit and the one after it become spaces (the exe's `bVar2`).
- The user's `~/Downloads/psobb-client/data/smutdata.prs` is 8 bytes (PRS-decodes to 16 zero bytes: group count 0). On that copy the filter is a no-op (count -1: copy).

**Port.**
- `client/src/net/simplemail.ts`: the tables; `normalizeFilterUnit`, `normalizeAndFilter` (0x813b18), `processEntityNameWithShopItems` (0x813a78), `filterMailBody` (the body's message, in place as the exe), `setShopDialogItems` (the exe's global list). `SimpleMailBox.receive` filters before the text check, as 007c8dc4 does. The header comment now gives 0x007c8dc4 and the correct pair-table path.
- `client/src/classic/main.ts`: `smutdata.prs` is read after the title file (not awaited; a missing file keeps the list empty); `enterGame` listens for `simpleMail` on the `Game` (the lobby is detached while in a game, so before this a mail in a game was dropped): the mail is stored in the session's box and plays SE 0x586 (`SE.newMail`).
- The auto reply. Exe: the answer text is `Session_GetAnswerServiceDataPointer_0077a5b0` = `FUN_006c1bd4(0xffff) + 0x2510`, where `FUN_006c1bd4` returns `DAT_00a95df8` (the current character data). So the text is in the character's save, at file offset **0x29EC** (0xAC units; newserv's PSOBBCharacterFile, the same as `charfile.ts`). The offset delta (+0x4DC) is the one the Info Board uses (0x2B44 / +0x2668, DEVLOG "Info Board"). Where it leaves the exe: C7 (`send_packet0xc7`, dump 812242) carries the text on close; the save goes to the server as E7 (`send_packet0xe7`, dump 811346: `calloc(0x399c)`, a full character file) from `send_packet5` (dump 811320: E7, then command 05). The port never sends E7 upstream.
- `client/src/net/charfile.ts`: `writeAutoReply(raw, text)` writes the 0xAC units at 0x29EC. `client/src/net/bbsession.ts`: the box starts with the save's `autoReply` (E7 is read before the lobby), and each new text (`setAnswerText`) is kept in `character.autoReply` and in the raw E7 copy (`keepAutoReply`).
- `tests/simplemail.test.ts`: section 7 (the filter: no list, a word, capitals, every occurrence, symbols in the text, fullwidth, the tab, two groups in turn, a word past the pattern, the 0081 path with and without the list) and section 8 (the save offset, the box's start text and its save hook, C7 on close).

**ASSUMED.**
- `FILTER_PASSES` (256): the exe loops until the word is gone; the port stops after 256 passes over one word (a replacement that rebuilds the word would hang the exe).
- O[-1] (the unit before the message, read by the exe when a match starts at the first unit) is taken as set, so the first unit is replaced.
- The tab rule (the unit after a tab is a space) is the decompile's `bVar2` reading; not checked against a Chrome run.
- Dispatch of 0x81 in a game (the pair table, not state-gated) and the SE / store of 007c8dc4's callee chain (carried from the entry above).
- smutdata.prs is loaded at start-up (InitializeShopDialog's caller not traced).
- The answer service starts off after a load whatever the saved text (the exe's flag bit 0 is not in the save).
- The save offset 0x29EC is the port's reading of the exe's +0x2510 with the Info Board's +0x4DC delta (two anchors, not a field decode).

**Left.**
- The E7 upload (`send_packet0xe7` / `send_packet5`): the answer text (and everything else) reaches the server only if the port sends E7. Not ported; the change lasts for the page's session.
- The smutdata list is not in the user's data copy (zero groups), so the filter is unobserved in Chrome. No Playwright run (per the brief).
- The Info Board line in ROADMAP still reads as a no-op (it was ported in the 13529 entry); not corrected here.

**Checks:** `node tests/simplemail.test.ts` (all pass, incl. sections 7 and 8); `node tests/symbolchat.test.ts`, `trade.test.ts`, `shop.test.ts`, `medical.test.ts` pass; `tests/items.test.ts` exits non-zero on the absent `vendor/newserv/build/newserv` (known); `client`: `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` clean (exit 0). The worktree's `client/node_modules` is a temporary symlink to the main checkout's, removed before the commit.


## 2026-10-23: keyboard controls audit against the manual, function-key shortcuts, auto run / walk

The official PSOBB keyboard map was checked row by row. `docs/CONTROLS.md` has the table: the manual's key, the exe role (input enum `unknown_input_type` in the named dump, line 86172, with the key config binding), the port status, and file:line.

**Exe.**
- `unknown_handle_fkey_inputs` (dump 682260) returns the menu entry a function key opens: F2 equipment (0x09), F3 technique (0x03), F4 MAG (0x17), F5 guild card (0x0E), F6 simple mail (0x13), F7 symbol chat (0x12), F8 team (0x25). Ctrl and Alt give none. Shift must be clear unless character option 0x2000000 is set, then it must be held. The entry goes through `ChallengeMenuObject_HandleItemSelection_00733714`, then `ValidateMenuItemCondition_00732620`, then `handle_player_menu_select`.
- F1 toggles the F-key help window (flags 0x200 / 0x400, `unknown_render_help_menu`). F9 / F10 are the team chat window (`TeamChatMenu_Update_00717260`, dump 678299 and 678385). F11 is `keyboard_controls_toggle` (dump 697159, character option 0x1000000).
- `unknown_handle_movement` (dump 667085..667215): the autorun and autowalk roles toggle `g_MouseControlsSetting_00a97f48` (off / run / walk), and while it is set the forward input is held at `move_speed`. Alt blocks the toggles.
- The presets (`PRESET_CODES`, `input/keyconfig.ts`) leave bindings 4 and 5 (autorun, autowalk) at 0 in all four presets, so the manual's Q and E are not the exe's defaults.

**Port.**
- `client/src/input/shortcuts.ts` (new): the F-key roles, the menu id per F-key, the field and lobby leaf sets, `functionKeyAction` (modifiers, shift option), `functionKeyNames` (live config).
- `client/src/input/automove.ts` (new): the auto run / walk state machine (edge toggles, a direction key turns it off) and its axes (run fb 128, walk fb 64).
- `client/src/input/keyconfig.ts`: roles `autorun` / `autowalk`; `bindingKey(i)`; `BINDING.functionKeyInfo` and `BINDING.mainMenu2`.
- `client/src/classic/fieldmenu.ts`: `openShortcut(id)`: F2..F4 open the leaf in the field, with the validation of the field menu.
- `client/src/render/fieldhud.ts`: the F-key path before the menu keys; F12 is read through the binding (`bindingKey(BINDING.mainMenu2)`), not the literal `'F12'`.
- `client/src/classic/lobby.ts`: F5..F8 open the lobby's guild card, mail, symbol list and team list (validated with the lobby's `lobbyMenuRules`); F12 through the binding.
- `client/src/render/lobbyview.ts`: Q / E (fallback keys) drive the auto move in the movement tick (the view the field uses too).
- `tests/shortcuts.test.ts` (new): the F-key mapping, the modifier and shift gates, rebinding, the field and lobby entry rules, the auto-move state machine. `tests/options.test.ts`: the `KEYS` expectation gains `autorun` / `autowalk`.

Brief: the user's GameCube reference of the field main menu (Home): dimmed striped background, the 3D view shrunk to a window top right, the list (Item Pack, Customize, Technique, Chat, Status, Options, Quit Game), a help window bottom left, and a character info panel bottom right (name, Lv, class, section ID, Total EXP, To Next Lv, Money, page 1/3 with L / R arrows). Port: `classic/fieldmenu.ts` and `classic/mainmenu.ts` (rows, help, view shift) and `render/fieldhud.ts` (attach: the projection shift). The reference is GC, not Blue Burst; only what PsoBB.exe does is ported.

**Exe evidence (PsoBB.exe, Ephinea 1.25.13; dump `Psobb.exe-05112026.c`; dump names checked against the data).**
- Main table 0x009f2f40 (`tools/exedata.py read 0x009f2f40 u 40`): 2 Item Pack (sub 0x009f2f80: 9, 0xb, 0x17, 0x1a, 0xc, 0xf), 0 Customize, 3 Technique, 5 Chat (sub 0x009f2fb8: 0x11, 0x12, 0xe, 0x13, 0x16, 0x15), 0x23 Team (sub 0x009f2ff0: 0x25, 0x27, 0x29, 0x2b, 0x2d), 6 Options, 7 Quit Game, end 0x30. The android table 0x009f3020 is from the dump's FUN_00733d70 comment (not re-read). So the BB row in the GC Status slot is **Team (0x23)**; no table holds 0x19 (Status).
- Status 0x19 (`player_status_menu`, dump `handle_player_menu_select` at 700118, case at 700321) builds `ChatShortcutMenuWindow_Constructor_00756ff4` (dump 727858): a 3-row sub-list (group 11 0x132..0x134). Its only caller is that switch case. The dispatch sources are the table walk (`handle_player_menu_inputs`, 699686), the fkey path (`unknown_handle_fkey_inputs`: 9, 3, 0x17, 0xe, 0x13, 0x12, 0x25 only), and the palette / UI-element actions (`UIManager_HandleElementAction_007181ec` called with 0x1d / 0x1e only). No path reaches 0x19. Its help text exists (group 0x0b 0x19 "Display player status, battle, and challenge grade."), which fits the GC Status row, not a BB row.
- Info strings (unitxt_e.prs, group 0x0b): 0x99 "Total EXP", 0x9a "To Next Lv", 0x9b "Money", 0x9c..0xa6 the stat labels (ATP..ELT), 0xa7 / 0xa8 "Battle", 0xa9..0xad the challenge labels. So the pages' texts exist in BB, but the only window that could use them is the unreachable 0x19 window (page 1 Total EXP / To Next / Money; page 2 stats; page 3 battle / challenge). The GC panel has the same texts, but BB has no caller for the panel itself. The equipment panel reads 0x9c.. too (`EquipmentStatDisplayObject_SetStatLabels_00726f38`), so those labels are not evidence for a page.
- Help text: one group 0x0b string per cursor row (FUN_0073249c; help window at entry 0x1c = (17, 312), 206 x 140). Row 2 is "Equip weapons or use items here." (0x0b:2), the same sentence the GC shows. The port does this (`MainMenu.help`).

The port's `menuViewShift` uses the same numbers (s = 1 - 80/320 t, the scale of the exe's projection relation).

- The F-key help list (`unknown_render_help_menu`, dump 682584: group 11 0x161..0x16c, 12 rows, toggled by a function key) is a key list, not the Home menu's info panel.

**GC vs BB (what differs).**

## 2026-10-23: EXP and HP floating texts (exe check)

Brief: the magenta "EXP+5" over a killed enemy and the green "HP+602" over healed players (vanilla references `images/5.png`, `images/6.png`). The premise was partly wrong per the exe, and both texts were already in the port (`classic/hud.ts` expText / hitText / FloatingTexts, `combat/hitfx.ts` restaFloat, `render/combat.ts` expPopup / Resta). This entry checks them against the exe and pins the timings in `tests/level.test.ts`.

**Exe evidence (PsoBB.exe, dump `Psobb.exe-05112026.c`).**
- EXP text: `handle_experience` (`.c:762698`) calls `display_special_attack_text_effect(&this->unknown_lockon_cursor_position, 0xffff00ff, 0x14, 0x14, u_EXP_009783a0, amount, player_idx)` (`.c:762739`). ARGB 0xffff00ff is magenta. Duration 0x14 is param 3; the delay 0x14 is param 4 (stored at object +0x60). The text is "EXP" + "+" when the amount is >= 0 + the number (`display_special_attack_text_effect` `.c:765648`).
- Amount (`.c:762716`..`762741`): bp xp * 13 when `g_CurrentEpisode == 1`, else * 10; then * 10 for the last attacker, * 8 for a tagger; the challenge multiplier; then `(iVar3 / 100) * unknown_xp_multiplier`. The port's `killExp` takes the same factors.
- 6xBF: `handle_packet0x60_subcommand0xbf` (`.c:574001`) calls vtable +0x30 = `add_to_player_exp_and_clamp` (`.c:575658`), which only adds and clamps. No text. The port's `onGiveExp` shows none either (correct).
- Object: `unknown_display_floating_text_effect` (`.c:765541`) stores colour & 0xffffff, duration at +0x5c, delay at +0x60, and the player index at +0x66 (< 4: drawn only on that slot's screen, else 0xffff: always). Update (`FloatingTextObject_Update_0078ab74`, `.c:765690`): counts the delay down, then rises and ages. Render (`FloatingTextObjectRender_0078abd0`, `.c:765712`): culled by a distance threshold (not on boss maps) and by a dot-product threshold (behind the camera), per glyph reveal and fade (alpha = age * 255 * 0.5, 0xff from the max distance).
- Green HP: `entity_hit_by_tech`, case `resta` (`.c:748189`): `CreateFloatingTextObject_0078a944(pos, 0xff00ff00, 0x14, 0, "HP"+"+"+n, n)`, so the delay is 0 and the duration 0x14, over the healed entity. The same call sits in the Volopt form-2 heal (`.c:187401`, 0x1e frames, boss only) and the Saint Milion drain (`.c:751448`, delay 10, `SaintEmilionMissile_SpawnFloatingText`, name from the dump, may be wrong).
- Items: the heal paths (`.c:437968`..`437986`, `.c:574615`..`574619`, `add_player_hp` in the 6x packet handler) make no floating text. The item heal shows no "HP+" text in the exe. (The level-up "HP+n" line, `display_levelup_stats` `.c:710876`, is a message-window line, not a floating text.)

**Port (already in place).** `expText` (magenta, delay 0x14, duration 0x14, sign), `hitText` (delay 0, duration 0x14, the damage number and Resta), `restaFloat` (green 0x00ff00), `expPopup` on the killer's client at the enemy's kill (`render/combat.ts`, both the boss and the normal kill), Resta's green text over the other healed players (`render/combat.ts` `resta`, `remoteResta`). Nothing changed in the drawer.

**Changes.** `tests/level.test.ts`: EXP colour and sign; a hit text (Resta / number) lives 0x14 frames with no delay. `docs/ROADMAP.md` (the HUD line), this entry.

**ASSUMED.**
- The EXP text's anchor: the exe uses the enemy's lock-on cursor position (`unknown_lockon_cursor_position`, the bloodstain-based height), the port uses the enemy's root + 22 (kept).
- The Resta text's anchor: the exe uses the hit entity's `position` argument; the port uses the player's position + 26 (kept).
- The local caster's own Resta: the port shows no green text over the caster (its comment says "every other healed player"); the exe's self-hit path was not traced.
- The render's distance cull and slot gate (the threshold floats are in the binary; their addresses are not in the dump) are not ported; with one local player the slot gate is always open.

**Checks.** `node tests/level.test.ts` (60 checks pass; the PlyLevelTbl cases skip without the table), `node tests/hitfx.test.ts` (pass), `cd client && npx tsc --noEmit -p .` (exit 0). No Playwright.

**Left.**

- The caster's own Resta text (see ASSUMED).
## 2026-10-23: Pioneer 2 in a game: palette and hotbar hidden on safe maps

**Report:** the 2026-10-23 "motion set and hub gates" entry left open whether the exe draws the action palette (3 slots, GUI 0x20 = (484, 368)) and the hotbar (GUI 0x21 = (0, 442)) on Pioneer 2. The creator and the map gate are now traced: the exe hides both on the safe maps. The port drew them on every floor; it now hides them on Pioneer 2, the Lab, the lobby and Episode 4's Pioneer 2.

**Exe evidence (PsoBB.exe, dump `reverse/refsrc/.../src/Psobb.exe-05112026.c`).**
- The windows are children of the quick menu window. `QuickmenuobjectConstructor_00716354` (dump 677373) is called from `CreateMapObjects_0078243f` (dump ~758825), so it is built on every map load. Its child constructor `SinowberillChallengeMenuWindow_Constructor_0071a3d0` (dump 681747) builds the palette at +0x38 (`CreateSinowberillChallengeObjectListItem_0070f6bc`, GUI 0x20, dump 671457) and the hotbar at +0x3c (`SinowberillChallengeObjectListWindow_Constructor_007104bc`, GUI 0x21, dump 672339), and sets object flag 0x4 (at +8 of each window) on both. Flag 0x4 is the hidden state.
- The update functions `unknown_update_player_menu_hide_palette` (dump 682035) and `unknown_update_player_menu_hide_hotbar` (dump 682072) return at once while the flag is set. They place the windows: palette y 368 (0x43b80000), 268 (0x43860000) with the main panel open; hotbar y 443 (0x43dd0000), 342 (0x43ab0000) with the panel open.
- Only one writer clears the flag: `unknown_update_player_menu_corner` (dump 681845), state 0x26 of the window's frame counter (`+0x1e`, starts at 0 on construction, so about 38 frames after the map load). It clears +0x38 and +0x3c only when `is_current_map_safe()` returns nonzero. The dump's name is inverted: `is_current_map_safe` (dump 820975) returns 0 when `current_map` is in the hub table `unknown_safe_maps` (0x0097f1c8 = 0, 15, 18, 45, -1; read with `tools/exedata.py read 0097f1c8 u 6`) and 1 otherwise. So the windows show on an unsafe map and stay hidden on a hub. The other clears of 0x4 in this range (681858, 677543) are on other windows (+0x34, the challenge list; +0x84 entries).
- Palette input follows the same flag: `unknown_handle_quickmenu` (dump ~682500) returns at once when the palette is hidden and the map is not the lobby.
- So: Pioneer 2 (map 0), the Lab (0x12), Episode 4's Pioneer 2 (0x2d) and the lobby (0x0f) show neither window; an unsafe map shows both. The palette's own slot-enable check (`is_palette_slot_use_allowed`, dump 597491) is unchanged (the attack slot stays enabled and the press is dropped, see the hub entry).
- Weapon: already hidden on the hubs (`UpdateItemVisibility_005c3f7c`, the DEVLOG 2026-10-23 weapon visibility entry), no change.

**Port.** `client/src/classic/fieldmenu.ts` `paletteWindowsShown(area)` = `!isSafeMap(area)` (the same table as the hub gate, `SAFE_MAPS`). `client/src/render/fieldhud.ts` draw: the palette (`paletteHud.draw`) and the hotbar (`drawHotbar`) are drawn only when it is true (and still only with the menu closed and no counter). The header comment of `render/fieldhud.ts` lists the rule.

**ASSUMED.**
- The render walker skips an object with flag 0x4 set. Not traced: the update functions use the flag and nothing in the windows' own render (`SinowberillChallengeObjectListWindow_Render_00731a40`, dump 699098) checks it.
- The port shows both at once on an unsafe map; the exe shows them after the counter's state 0x26 (about 38 frames after the map load). A short delay is not modelled.
- The palette's Ctrl flip (`HandlePlayerPaletteToggle_00694f0c`) is not gated by the map in the port; the exe's flip path was not traced for the hidden state (the flip is invisible on a hub, so the port keeps it).

**Tests:** `tests/fieldhud.test.ts` (new check: `paletteWindowsShown` on 0, 0x0f, 0x12, 0x2d, 1, 0x0d, 0x17). Run with Node 24 and `client/node_modules` linked from the main checkout for the run (removed after): `node tests/fieldhud.test.ts`, `tests/telepipe.test.ts`, `tests/hotbar.test.ts`, `tests/lobbymenu.test.ts`, `tests/battletraps.test.ts`, `tests/minimap.test.ts`, `tests/questboard.test.ts`, `tests/shortcuts.test.ts`, `tests/windowanim.test.ts`, `tests/options.test.ts`, `tests/controls.test.ts` all pass. `cd client && npx tsc --noEmit -p .` clean. No Playwright (the brief); no Chrome screenshot of Pioneer 2 or Forest 1.

## 2026-10-23: Meet the User reconnects (the 0041 reply's embedded 19)

**Premise checked against the exe.** The entry above said the port stays on its block and the embedded 0x19 is not sent. The exe does both, so this entry ports the reconnect. The Send Mail and Meet the User leaves are otherwise as the previous entry says.

**Exe evidence (PsoBB.exe, Psobb.exe-05112026.c dump):**
- State 0x12 (dump 721093) calls `ChallengePlayerInfoWindow_ProcessPhaseLabel_0074f028` (dump 722132). It returns unless the list's reply flag (+0x94 bit 1) is set. It copies the location (+0xc0, packet +0x24) cut at 0x44 units, keeps the last `,` token as `g_SinowberillChallengePhaseLabel`, and then calls `ShipConnectionManager_HandlePacket0x19_007d7640(g_pShipConnectionManager, list+0xb0, list+0x148)`.
- The list copy (`ChallengePlayerInfoWindowListWindow_UpdateContent_0074ef0c`, dump 722063) is the 0x130-byte 0041 packet from its header, at list+0x9c. So list+0xb0 is packet +0x14 (the embedded 19, header then body) and list+0x148 is packet +0xac (0x84 bytes, the Meet User extension).
- `ShipConnectionManager_HandlePacket0x19_007d7640` (dump 812031): sends the embedded 19 with `send_packet` on the current connection (`*param_1` bytes); reads the address from `param_1[2]` (packet +0x1c) and the port from `param_1[3]` low 16 bits (packet +0x20); copies the 0x84 extension to `g_Packet0x19Data_00aaec20`; calls the connection's vtable +0x14 (close), sets +0x12138 = 1 (the reconnect flag), +0x1211c / +0x12130 / +0x1641c / +0x16420 = 0, sets the target (`DarvantForm7Target_SetPhaseId` / `SetTargetId`), calls vtable +0x10 (connect; a negative result sets +0x10074), then vtable +0x18 (on connected).
- The reconnect login: `handle_ship_packet0x3` (dump 813403) sends the 0xB4-byte 93 login and, when +0x12138 is set, goes to socket state 6 (`g_SocketState = '\x06'`, dump line 813510) with the extension stored in `_DAT_00a46bfc`. The names of that global are wrong (only written here); the 93 body is not traced byte by byte.
- The packet layout matches newserv `S_GuildCardSearchResultT` (vendor/newserv/src/CommandFormats.hh; the BB form is 0x128 after the 8-byte header): player tag +8, searcher +0xc, result +0x10, embedded header +0x14 (8 bytes), embedded reconnect body +0x1c (address big-endian, port, unused), location +0x24 (0x44 units), extension +0xac (`SC_MeetUserExtensionT`: lobby_refs[0] menu_id +0xac, item_id +0xb0, name +0xf0 (0x20 units)). `handle_ship_packet0x41` (dump 809943) copies the same 0x130 bytes.
- newserv's 93 (`C_LoginBase_BB_93`, 0x7C): connection_phase 6 is "lobby server (with Meet User fields specified)"; menu_id at 0x74 and preferred_lobby_id at 0x78 are the lobby ref; `on_93_BB` (ReceiveCommands.cc) takes the lobby when menu_id is `MenuID::LOBBY` (0x33000033).

**Port:**
- `client/src/net/guildcard.ts`: `parseSearchResult` also returns `reconnect` (embedded flag and the 8 body bytes at payload 0x14) and `phaseLabel`; `phaseLabelOf(location)` is the ProcessPhaseLabel token rule (last non-empty `,` token, cut at 0x10 units).
- `client/src/net/bbconnection.ts`: `LoginParams.menuId` / `preferredLobbyId` are written at body 0x74 / 0x78 (they were zero).
- `client/src/net/bbsession.ts`: `BBSession.meetUser(reply)` sends the embedded 19 on the current connection, opens the reply's port (`open`, as `followRedirect`), logs in with connection_phase 6, menu_id `MENU_ID_LOBBY` and the reply's lobby (`itemId`), waits for 67, rebinds the guild card sync, mailbox and info board to the new connection (`guildCardSync = null`, then `startGuildCardSync`), and returns the new `Lobby`.
- `client/src/classic/teammenu.ts`: `TeamHost.meetMember?(card)`; Enter on Meet the User calls it once (the phase label starts as before).
- `client/src/classic/main.ts`: `teamHost(lobby, shipName)` keeps the last 0041 reply (`memberReply`, set by `searchMember`); `meetMember` calls `session.meetUser(reply)` and then `enterLobby(next, shipName)`, which shows the new lobby screen.
- `tests/guildcard.test.ts`: the embedded 19 body bytes, its flag, the phase label, the LOBBY ref, and `phaseLabelOf` (empty, no comma, empty tokens, the 0x10 cut). `tests/teammenu.test.ts`: `meetMember` gets the searched card once; a key during the phase label does not ask again.

**ASSUMED:**
- The embedded 19 is sent back to the server with the reply's 8-byte header flag and the 8 body bytes (length 0x10, as newserv's reconnect header). The exe sends `*param_1` bytes; the length and flag were not checked against a live reply. newserv has no client-side 19 handler (grep found none), so the echo is assumed harmless there.
- The reconnect login uses connection_phase 6 with menu_id LOBBY and the reply's lobby as preferred_lobby_id. The exe's 93 body was not decoded; the phase and lobby fields follow newserv's documentation of the Meet User login.
- The reply's address is not used. `connectBridge(port)` routes every port to the bridge's server, as `followRedirect` already does. A real multi-server setup would need the address.
- The ship connection's vtable slots (+0x14 close, +0x10 connect, +0x18 connected) are named by their order in `HandlePacket0x19` and in the matching `handle_ship_packet0x19` (dump 201495); their bodies were not traced.
- `startGuildCardSync` is once per session in the port; for Meet it is reset so the guild card client, mailbox and info board use the new connection. The exe's per-lobby sync was not traced.
- The member list's 450-frame wait still runs on the old lobby screen; the new screen replaces it when the reconnect finishes. If the reconnect takes longer than 450 frames, the list closes first and the old screen stays until the new lobby is shown. The old screen's pings during the reconnect are not stopped.
- `parseSearchResult`'s `address` is still read as little-endian u32; newserv writes it big-endian. It is not used for the connection.

**Not ported / left:**
- **Guild Card search result (player info) Meet row:** the port's Guild Card window has no Meet row, and the exe's Guild Card result window was not traced. The reconnect helper (`BBSession.meetUser`) is reusable for it; the row and its state are the missing part.
- **The phase label is not drawn:** its only reader in the dump is the Sinowberill challenge timer (`BuildPhaseTimerString_0077ba70`, dump 752612), which the port does not have. It is kept on the parsed reply (`phaseLabel`).
- **Sent Item (state 0x15)** is still greyed (trade item window, not traced).
- Not run live: no second player or multi-ship server in this session. The 93 phase 6 login and the 19 echo are checked only against newserv's source and the exe's control flow.

**Checks:** `node tests/teammenu.test.ts` (ALL PASS, 155 checks), `node tests/guildcard.test.ts` (ALL PASS), `node tests/guildcardmenu.test.ts`, `node tests/simplemail.test.ts`, `node tests/lobbymenu.test.ts`, `node tests/lobbymain.test.ts`, `node tests/team.test.ts` (all pass). `client` `tsc --noEmit -p .` clean (Node 24; the worktree's `client/node_modules` symlink is removed before the commit).

Scope: the main menu's Customize row (menu id 0, "Customizes the Action Menu.") and the E7 save upload that the exe makes on leaving the session. Client code and tests; the server side is newserv (vendor/newserv, read only).

**Premise check.** The brief said the exe sends E7 on leave. Confirmed, with more triggers than leave (see the E7 part). The palette is NOT saved by E7 on this server: the palette save is 07ED (below), and newserv's E7 handler keeps neither the palette nor the auto reply.

### Customize window (exe)

- Menu entry: `customize_menu1` / `customize_menu2` (menu id 0) at dump 700143: `customize_menu_constructor` (dump 717277), with the window's flag +0x24 and the two lists.
- Lists: the slot list at GUI position table entry 0x0F = (0, 256) (`CreateGuildCardListWindow_00748d8c`, dump 717602, `get_gui_position(0xf)`); the action list at entry 0x10 = (214, 256) (`customize_menu_action_list_constructor`, dump 718599, `get_gui_position(0x10)`); table 0x00971f40, 8-byte stride (`tools/exedata.py read 00971fb8 f 4`). Titles: unitxt group 11 0x36 (slot list) and 0x35 (action list). The dump's `GuildCardListWindow*` names are the customize window's (the names are wrong, the code is the customize window).
- Input (`unknown_handle_customize_menu_inputs`, dump 717334): state machine in +0x1c (2 = slot list, 3 / 4 = action list). Keys: Decide (g_KeyboardSharedState[0xc] | [0x15]) and Cancel ([0xd]). In the action list the number keys 1..0 (`was_input_pressed` with 0x23..0x2c, the palette_bar_slot enum) write hotbar slot iVar8 = 4..13 (flat palette_slots index 3..12) from the highlighted row (dump 717401..717443).
- Palette data: `get_palette_data_for_customize` (dump 555029) returns the regular palette (`currently_casting_tech_info + 0xd8`, the 0xE8 config); the pb palette branch is unused (the dump's own comment says so).
- Hotbar write (`unknown_set_palette_slot`, dump 558003, writes group_1 and group_2 only): the toggle (the row equals palette 0's slot) clears the slot in BOTH palettes (717407..717410); otherwise every other hotbar slot with the row's action is cleared in both palettes (717427..717436) and the slot takes the action in both palettes (717438..717439).

## 2026-10-23: chat shortcuts (Shift+F), Log Window page keys, text chat cooldown

**What changed.** The F keys in the chat form and Shift+F send the save's chat shortcut slots (text or symbol chat), with the shared chat cooldown. PageUp / PageDown scroll the lobby's Log Window by a page. Text chat (typed lines) now waits for the same cooldown, and the End-key picker shares the timer with it. `input/shortcuts.ts` (`chatShortcutIndex`, `chatFormOption`, the corrected comment on the option), `net/chatshortcut.ts` (new: the 16 BB records at 0x1FAC), `classic/chat.ts` (`ChatLog.page` / `back` / `wrapped`, `logWindowRows`, `ChatLine.cooldownOver` / `startCooldown` / `tickCooldown` / `useShortcut` / `sendSymbol`, the held typed line), `classic/field.ts` (the picker uses the chat line's timer; `sendSymbolChat`), `classic/lobby.ts` (the tick, the Log Window keys, the shortcut keys), `render/fieldhud.ts` (the chat slot key, the option on the menu path), `render/gameview.ts` (the `chatShortcut` hook). Not done: the Chat > Shortcut leaf editor.

**Premise corrections (per the exe).**
- `CONTROLS.md` said PageUp / PageDown had no exe handler. The keys are raw keycodes, not input roles: `pso_keycode` page_up = 8, page_down = 9 (dump line 2810), read with `was_key_pressed_no_modifiers` in the list-window input (dump 724833 / 724837, `ChallengePlayerListWindow_HandleInput_00752238`, 724757). The Log Window is built by `chat_log_menu` (dump 700284), which calls `ChallengePlayerListWindow_Constructor_00752114`, whose vtable 0x00b42448 has slot 1 = 0x00752238 (`tools/exedata.py read 0x00b42448 u 16`).
- The Shift+F option was taken as "not in the port". It is the character option 0x2000000 (Function Key), and the port reads it now (option_flags at 0x4EC; bit 0x1000000 is keyboard controls, `newserv` SaveFileFormats.hh 586..590).
- Text chat had no cooldown (DEVLOG 2026-10-23, the End picker entry). The exe gates it: the chat window's send row calls `send_chat_message_with_cooldown` (724794, with the row's 0x10 flag retried each frame). ASSUMED that the typed line uses that row (see below).
- The dump's class names are wrong in places: the Log Window is a "ChallengePlayerList" constructor, and the "ChatShortcutMenuYesNoListWindow" family is the generic list window. The behaviour above is from the code paths, not the names.

**Exe evidence** (`refsrc/original-psobb-client-source/src/Psobb.exe-05112026.c`):
- `handle_chat_shortcuts` (674857): returns when the 0x8 flag is set, a UI panel is visible, a menu is open, Ctrl or Alt is held. The option test: option 0x2000000 clear requires Shift, set requires no Shift. Then `was_key_pressed(f1..f12)` in order, `use_chat_shortcut(0..10)` and `(0xb)` for F12. The chat reader uses raw F keys (pso_keycode f1 = 64 .. f12 = 75), not the key config's bindings.
- `unknown_handle_fkey_inputs` (682260), the menu reader, has the mirror test on Shift (clear: no Shift; set: Shift). So the two readers split the same keys by the option: the default (clear) gives plain F = menu and Shift+F = chat; set gives plain F = chat and Shift+F = menu. This matches newserv's comment ("0 = menu shortcuts; 1 = chat shortcuts").
- `use_chat_shortcut` (754183) -> `get_chat_shortcut_optcall` (754134: a 0xa4 stride from the session block) -> `send_chat_message_with_cooldown_optcall` (754207). The timer is set before `send_chat_message` (754259), so an empty record starts it too (type 0 sends nothing).
- `send_chat_message` dispatches type 1 to `send_chat_message_text` (754354: an empty line returns; otherwise `send_packet6` in the logged-in scene), type 2 to `send_chat_message_word_select` (664328, not ported), type 3 to `send_chat_message_symbol_chat` (754781).
- The cooldown: `is_chat_message_cooldown_over` (679808: the short at `g_pUITextColorTable + 0x22` below 1), `set_chat_message_cooldown_timer` (679819: 0x2d). The shortcut path does not retry: a refused record is dropped.
- The shortcut records: `get_chat_shortcut_optcall` = `&puVar1[0xc].field_0x180 + index * 0xa4`. newserv's `SaveFileShortcutEntryBB` is 0xA4 bytes: u32 type at +0, the definition at +4 (UTF-16 text 0x50 chars, or a SymbolChatT). `PSOBBCharacterFile.shortcuts` at 0x1FAC, 0x10 entries (0x1ACC + 12 x 0x68 = 0x1FAC).
- The Log Window's page step: `ListWindow_UpdateRenderProgress_0073c554` (707846) adds to +0xa4 and the keys add -380.0 / +380.0. `ChatShortcutMenuYesNoListWindow_AddItem_0073c228` (707658) -> `SyncRenderState_0073b5e0` sets +0xa4 to 0, so a new line returns the view to the newest (the port's `ChatLog.add`). The clamp is `ClampRenderPosition_0073f8a4` (710748); the animation (the +0x50 state) is not traced into the port.

**Ported:**
- Chat shortcuts: a slot is sent with the cooldown (text: `lobby.sendChat` / `game.sendChat`; symbol: `game.sendSymbolChat` in the field with the sender's balloon). The field HUD's key handler checks the slot before the menu, the lobby's key handler after the menu shortcuts. Ctrl / Alt: none. A menu or the chat input open: none.
- Typed text: Enter sends and starts the cooldown. Enter during the cooldown holds the line (the input stays open with its text, Space does nothing, Escape drops it); it goes when the cooldown ends.
- The End-key picker's timer is the chat line's (`ChatLine.cooldownOver`), so one timer gates all sends.
- PageUp / PageDown in the lobby's Log Window: a page (380 px = 19 rows of 20 px) per press, clamped to the lines that exist; PageUp shows older lines.

**ASSUMED** (also in `docs/CONTROLS.md`):

- The cooldown ticks every 30 Hz frame in the lobby and the field. The exe ticks it only while the quick menu's chat panel is up (677732, the existing ASSUMED).
- The Log Window's animation is applied at once; the page is 380 px = 19 rows (one visible page); PageUp is older lines.
- The shortcut records are the ones the server sent at login (the save): the port has no editor and does not send E7 upstream.
- Raw F keys for the chat slots (`was_key_pressed(f1..f12)`).
- Word-select records send nothing; the lobby sends no symbol chat (the port's lobby has no symbol sender, the field has one).
- The field has no Log Window leaf (menu 0x15 is not in the port's field menu), so the page keys do nothing there.

Existing and passing under Node 24: `symbolchat`, `fkeys`, `fieldhud`, `lobbymenu`, `controls`, `emotes`. `cd client && npx tsc --noEmit -p .` exit 0 (with client/node_modules linked from the main checkout for the run, removed before the commit). ## 2026-10-23: Grants and Megid: the map ray

**What changed.** The Megid orb now stops at the map: the flight's ray from the old point to the new one (`combat/techlightning.ts` `MegidFlight.tick(candidates, wall)`, `MEGID_WALL_MASK` 0x100) moves it to the hit point and ends it. Before, the port flew through walls. The same ray serves the player's orb (`render/techlightning.ts` `TechWorld.wall`, `render/combat.ts` `techWall`) and the enemies' Megid (`MegidOrb`, a new last argument), through the game view's `wallHit` option (`render/gameview.ts`, `CollisionWorld.segmentHit` with the mask, returning the hit point). Grants needed no change: the constructor, stats, tracker, sounds and the 31st-update hit were re-traced and match the port (`GrantsTimeline`).

**Exe evidence** (named dump `refsrc/.../Psobb.exe-05112026.c`, values read with `tools/exedata.py read`):
- `update_megid` (line 648165): the emitter loop (copies the object's point to each particle; flag 4 would offset it by (0, 0, -5) turned by the yaw, and no tier sets flag 4), then `TechniqueEntity_UpdatePosition_006f0474`, `TechniqueEntity_CheckDuration_006f053c`, `TechniqueEntity_UpdateTargeting_006f0798`, in that order: the ray runs first, the hit test after it, on the same update.
- `UpdateTechniqueEntityPositionWithRaycast_006f04c0` (line 652470): `cast_ray_at_map_collision_geometry(old, new, 0x100)`. On a hit the position becomes the ground info's object point, vtable +0x10 is called and the ended flag (+8 bit 0) is set. `old` is +0x78..+0x80, saved by the position update.
- `cast_ray_at_map_collision_geometry` (line 756928) and `line_segment_intersects_triangle` (line 757050): with `unk_enum` 0 the nearest front face on the segment writes its intersection point into `g_CurrentGroundObject` (x/y/z), so the hit point is that point.
- The tier emitter table at 0x0096da78 (pointer and count pairs; 0xc-byte entries {id, flags, param}): tier 0 `1c5 1c8` flags 0; tiers 1-2 the same with flag 0x40 and scales 1.4 / 1.8; tiers 3-4 add `1c4` (flag 2) and scales 2.2 / 2.6; tier 5 adds `1c7` and `1cf` (flags 0x1002), scale 3. No entry has flag 0x20 (no model).
- `UpdateTargeting` (line 652631): the candidate is the first entry of `UpdateAoECollision_006ea7c4` (up to 15, EntityArray order; the function always returns its list), `is_npc_targetable` gates the hit, and `MegidEntity_ProcessHit_006ea310` skips a player already in its list of 32. The port's rule (first overlapping entity, struck list) matches.
- Megid's sounds (`PlayMegidSoundEffects_006e9d24`, line 647956): SE 0x92 by tier: 0 +0x100, 1 none, 2-3 -0x180, 4 -0x250 (as `TECH_PITCH`).
- Grants (`UpdateTechniqueTargetingEntity_006e6efc`, line 645959): the tracker is made only when the target is valid and the counter is 0, at the target's position (fixed), with flag 0x10 emitters, SE 0x93 with the tier's pitch (0x100 / none / -0x180 / -0x180 / -0x250 / -0x100), and the hit goes through `UpdateCastGrantEffectEffect_006e6ec0` on the 31st update.

**ASSUMED:**
- The orb's end callback (vtable +0x10 on a wall hit) is not decoded; the port only ends the flight (no visible effect is known for it).
- The enemy orb (`MegidOrb`) takes the same ray: its caster is the same TechniqueEntity; no separate enemy path was read.
- The map ray uses the port's `segmentHit` (face-flag mask, nearest front face), the same rule as the gun's `0x8100` wall test.

**Checks:** `node tests/techlightning.test.ts` (new: the ray runs from the old to the new point; a wall at z 8 ends the orb at its hit point; the entity at the hit point is hit on the wall update; an enemy orb stops at the wall), `techfire`, `techniques`, `hitfx`, `gunbullet`, `enemyfsmruins` pass; `cd client && npx tsc --noEmit -p .` exit 0. `tests/combat.test.ts` needs `vendor/newserv/build/newserv` (not built in this worktree, not run). Not run in Chrome.

**Left:** Megid's tier 3-5 two-point emitters (`0x1c4` flag 2, `0x1cf` flag 0x1002): `create_particle_effect2` takes a second vector, the object's angles (`+0x54` / `+0x5c`, from `Vector3f_GetAnglesZ` of the direction), which the particle engine has no orientation for (the same gap as Foie's flag 2 entries); the cast light on the caster (`CAST_LIGHT`, not drawn); the Galgryphon's and Jungle Tank trap's bolts.
## 2026-10-23: Home menu view shift (correction: it reaches the field's draw)

The entry above says the 3D view is not shifted in Chrome. That was a misreading of the screenshot. The shift is applied and drawn; the scene fills the canvas because the shifted frustum shows more of the room, not because the shift is missing. The root cause was not a missing wire.

**Chrome probe (`client/e2e/field-menu-home.spec.ts` and a temporary probe, not committed).** Closed: `camera.projectionMatrix` elements [0] 0.992, [5] 1.764, [8] 0, [9] 0; the render loop runs (`renderer.info.render.frame` 308 -> 470 in one second). Open (shift 3): [0] 0.744 and [5] 1.323 (both x 0.75), [8] -0.25, [9] -0.48. The projection the field's `renderer.render` uses is the shifted one. Pixel check: with the menu closed the player's feet are at about (640, 640); open they are at about (800, 400). The NDC map (0.75 x + 0.25, 0.75 y + 0.48) predicts (792, 398). So the room is drawn right and up at scale 0.75.

**Exe (PsoBB.exe, dump `render_player_menu_background`, 700858).** On open the globals are 80.0 and 115.2 (0x00a9a894 / 0x00a9a890 at the open branch), and the frame counter (param+0x60 / +0x61) runs 0..3. The centre written to the camera's UI struct is `x = (ViewportWidth >> 1) + (80 * scale / 3) * f` and `y = (ViewportHeight >> 1) - (115.2 * scale / 3) * f`, with the height's half 240 (the minus is in the formula, `-(fVar5 / fVar6) * fVar4 + (H >> 1)`). So the exe moves the centre **right and up** (y is screen-down). The brief's "right/down" is not the exe's. The scale is `a4 = (W - x) / (W / 2)` (0.75 at f = 3) and `a8 = y / (H / 2)` (0.52); the code keeps the larger (`if a8 <= a4`), so one uniform scale of 0.75. The port's NDC offsets (+0.25, +0.48) and scale 0.75 are the same numbers.

**Port.** `client/src/render/viewshift.ts` `applyMenuViewShift(cam, f)` is the one projection step (rebuild, premultiply the offset and scale, keep the inverse). The field's `FieldHud.attach` (`render/fieldhud.ts`) and the lobby's `applyViewShift` (`classic/lobby.ts`) call it; they had two copies of the same four lines. No behaviour change in the lobby.

**Screenshot.** `client/test-results/field-menu-home.png` (Home held 200 ms, menu open): the room and the player sit right and up of the closed frame, the menu panel and the help window are on the left. The closed frame is `client/test-results/zz-closed.png` from the probe run (the same character).

**Test.** `tests/viewshift.test.ts`: frame 0 projects the axis to the centre; frame 3 projects it to NDC (0.25, 0.48) (exe centre 400, 125 of 640 x 480); the frustum's edges go to -0.5 and +1.0 (scale 0.75 with the offset); applying a frame twice does not compound; frame 0 returns to the plain projection; projection times inverse is the identity. `node tests/viewshift.test.ts` and `node tests/mainmenulayout.test.ts` pass. `cd client && npx tsc --noEmit -p .` is clean. Playwright `e2e/field-menu-home.spec.ts` passes in Chrome.

**Worktree set-up (for the next run in a worktree).** The Vite config reads the newserv keys from `../vendor/newserv` next to `client/`, and the client needs `client/node_modules`; a worktree has neither, so both were symlinked from the main checkout for the runs and removed before the commit. Playwright needs Node 24 on PATH (the `npx` shebang picks Node 16 otherwise). Without the keys the login stops with "key file default.nsk not found".

**ASSUMED.**
- The exe draws the 3D view over the whole canvas at scale 0.75 (no viewport clip). The dump sets the centre and the scale only; the draw code was not traced, so a window-shaped view (as in the GC reference) is not ruled out.
- The room covers the canvas in the open frame because the scene is bigger than the shifted frustum (an inference from the projection; not checked against the exe's picture).

**Left.** Nothing for the shift. The GC reference's shrunk window is not reproduced (not in the exe's code path read here).

- Beam init (state 6/7 enter, `objdump` 0x0045A770 / 0x0045A790): the running point P = body position scaled to MaxScale (`+0x418/+0x420` = body x/z, then `normalize * [0x00A4577C]`); the heading D is the unit vector to the target (`+0x400/+0x408`, `vec3_sub` with the body, `0x82F9C4`; the copied source words are `+0x3bc/+0x3c0/+0x3c4`, which do not match the Transform's `+0x3c0`/`+0x3c8` cell centre: ASSUMED, see below); the side V = (`int_sin`, `int_cos`) of the heading (`fpatan` in int units, `65536/2pi`) plus `+0x4000` for state 6 and `-0x4000` for state 7 (`+0x40c/+0x414`).
- Constants (written by the init at 0x00459F00): MaxScale `[0x00A4577C]` = 230 + 50 = 280, multiplier `[0x00A45780]` = 50, ball scale `[0x00900200]` = 20, the damp of the minion `[0x009044B8]` = 0.995 and accel `[0x009044BC]` = 0.01.
- Per ball (`UpdateVoloptForm7Hazard`, dump 197587, the branch `+0x3d0 == 6 || 7` with the even counter in 4..38): `local = V * 20 + P`; the icon at `local` (`unknown_add_minimap_icon3(&local_64, 0xffffa24c, 0x40200000, 1, 1)`, dump 197706); the object: `RabartaInit_006ec8ec(local)` (state 6) or `CreateRafoieEffectEntity_006ed87c(local)` (state 7); `V = -V`; if `|P| > 280` then P is put on the ring and D becomes `-(sin, cos)` of the point's own heading (`b_minus_a(dir, pos) + dir = pos`, `b_minus_a` is `second - first`, `0x007A900C`); then `P += D * 50`.
- Minion (`UpdateGalgryphonMinion_004ab283`, dump 229526): the icon call (dump 229625) is after the state-2 branch returns, so it is in **state 1** (MOVE), not state 2. State 1: no ground under it (`unknown_get_ground_info`) -> dead; height = min(ground, 6) (`0x00903AE0`); timer > 0x168 -> state 2, timer 0; then (on the same tick) the velocity `(dir * 0.01 + v) * 0.995` per axis, the position += velocity, the icon at the new position, timer + 1. `dir` = the unit vector to the target player (`CalculateGalgryphonMinionEffectDirection_004ab4e8`, zero with no target). State 2: timer > 0x3c -> dead, else timer + 1.

**Ported:**
